title: Agents
tagline: Function calling, agent loops, planning, memory, code execution, multi-agent systems and agent security
summary: Language models become agents when they can act: call tools, run code, browse and operate computers over many steps. This course covers function calling, agent loops and planning, memory and context management, code and computer use, multi-agent systems, the evaluation of agents, and the security risks of autonomous action.

chapters.title: Function calling and tools
chapters.summary: Tool schemas, calling conventions and training models to use tools.

chapters.title: Agent loops
chapters.summary: ReAct, observation–action cycles and the design of agent scaffolds.

chapters.title: Planning and task decomposition
chapters.summary: Plans and subgoals, reflection, and recovering from errors.

chapters.title: Memory and context management
chapters.summary: Short- and long-term memory, summarisation and context engineering.

chapters.title: Code generation and execution
chapters.summary: Code models, sandboxes, software-engineering agents and their benchmarks.

chapters.title: Browsing and computer use
chapters.summary: Web agents, control of graphical interfaces and perception of screens.

chapters.title: Multi-agent systems
chapters.summary: Orchestrators and workers, and debate and cooperation between agents.

chapters.title: Agent evaluation and security
chapters.summary: Benchmarks for agents, reliability, prompt injection and permissions.
